extracted.intended_audience: news agency managers, newsroom editors, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and standards for handling wire-service (Associated Press/International News Service) material in newsroom operations, including confidentiality, physical control, timeliness, accuracy, and enforcement of rules. Drawn from affidavits and managerial statements describing duties and rules in a newsroom and news-service context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-staff access to wire-service material
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No person whatsoever, who was not a member of the staff of the New York American, should have any access whatsoever to any of the information, reports or news, supplied by The Associated Press to the New York American.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigid office rule: outsiders must be prevented from having access to AP (or similar) reports, bulletins, or despatches; applies at all times in editorial/news departments. Physical and supervisory measures should be used to enforce this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on internal disclosure to outsiders
rubrics_metrics.description: 'No member of the staff of the New York American, nor any of its employees, should disclose to any person outside of the New York American, and then only in the course of the preparation of the paper for publication, any of the information or news whatsoever received from The Associated Press.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff may only share wire-service material as strictly necessary for preparing the paper for publication; any other disclosure is forbidden. This defines a narrow permitted-use exception for publication prep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial duty to take immediate summary action on disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher/manager had 'full authority and power to take summary action to prevent any abuse or any improper use of the news matter furnished by The Associated Press, and I should have exercised that power drastically ... if I had been informed, or had any reason to believe, that employees ... were improperly ... permitting outsiders ... access.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers are expected to investigate allegations promptly and to use disciplinary or summary measures to stop and deter unauthorized disclosures; active enforcement is part of duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to refuse others access to proofs and telegraphic copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Manager 'immediately notified the foreman of the composing room that he should under no circumstances permit any agent or employee of the International News Service to obtain any proofs of telegraphic news printed in the New York American.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical control of proofs and telegraphic printouts: foremen and compositors must be instructed to deny proofs to competitors or outsiders; retain custody until publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security and monitoring of wire-receiving equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Morkrum machines 'are located in a small, partitioned room' and editors' desks were sited 'in full view' so staff 'was in a position to observe all persons who entered the editorial rooms ... especially those who approached the desks where the Associated Press matter was deposited and handled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site receiving equipment in a partitioned, controllable location; position desks and observers to detect unauthorized approach; use layout as part of access control and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express prohibition on attempting to obtain competitors' dispatches
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees were 'instructed ... that they were, under no circumstances whatever, to make any attempt to gain access to or knowledge of The Associated Press despatches delivered to the New York American, or to even look at the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond forbidding sharing, prohibit any active attempts by employees to access competitor wire dispatches (including looking at them); training and repeated instruction expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of collected news until publication by members
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is also important that the news collected by the defendant shall remain confidential and secret until its publication has been fully accomplished by all of the defendant's members.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services and agencies should keep collected news secret until all subscribing members have had their opportunity to publish; preventing early leakage preserves commercial value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not furnish news to non‑subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is essential 'that such news ... shall not be furnished to other newspapers which do not subscribe to the defendant's service and which do not pay therefor ... otherwise competing newspapers ... would unfairly and inequitably receive the benefit of its service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict distribution to paying subscribers; sharing with non-subscribers undermines the business model and is considered improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / speedy delivery is essential to news value
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is of the utmost importance that the defendant shall furnish and deliver to its customers the information and matters of news which it has collected as speedily as possible ... The speedy delivery of this matter is, of course, essential to its news value.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational metric: speed of collection-to-delivery is critical. Systems, staffing, and leased wires should be organized to minimize delay; competitive advantage depends on early delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive parity on release time
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is also essential that the news of the day shall be transmitted by the defendant to its subscribers as early or earlier than similar information can be furnished to other competing newspapers by other news-services.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to deliver news no later than competitors; measure performance against rival services and prioritize rapid transmission to subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and impartiality as core value drivers
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The value of the news service ... largely depends upon the promptness of its service and the accuracy and impartiality of its news, inasmuch as the newspapers served by the defendant are of all varieties and shades of political opinion and news policy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational quality criteria: ensure fact-checking and neutral presentation; accuracy and perceived impartiality protect reputation across diverse client political stances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful and independent sourcing (no improper appropriation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant's officers and employés 'have not ... been engaged ... in the practice of obtaining, unlawfully or improperly, news which The Associated Press has gathered ... nor have the defendant's employés been engaged ... in improperly appropriating such news.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain lawful sourcing practices; do not arrange with rival-paper staff to receive competitor material pre-publication. Documentation of independent sourcing and rewrites is important for legal defence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible re-writing of items from other newspapers when justified
rubrics_metrics.description: The defendant 'reads each day a great number of newspapers for items of news therein contained which have not been received by the defendant through other sources, and, as does every other ... rewrites for publication any news therein contained which it deems of sufficient importance to interest its subscribers, and as rewritten, furnishes such subscribers therewith.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable practice: monitoring other publications and rewriting items for subscribers is permitted if the agency rewrites and adds value; importance threshold should justify redistribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial accountability to promulgate and enforce rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I shall ... thoroughly investigate the charges ... and I shall immediately take adequate measures ... I will not only promulgate rules for the government of the employees ... but I will give the execution and enforcement of those rules my personal attention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must both create explicit policies governing access and handling of wire material and personally ensure their enforcement; investigation and corrective measures are required when breaches are alleged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial duty to examine and veto copy for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: As Night Editor 'it was my duty ... to examine, reject or pass for publication, "copy" of news matter for publication in the New York American, inclusive of "copy" prepared from the information furnished the American by the Associated Press.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are responsible for gatekeeping: review incoming wire copy, decide what to publish, rewrite if necessary, and ensure any use of wire material complies with rules and publication needs.
